summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 7.28% YoY to INR 133.66 crore and PAT grew 14% to INR 29.28 crore, while growth depends on GPU capacity going live from Q3.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 133.66 crore, up 7.28% YoY but down 20.20% QoQ, which management attributed to design services booked in a subsidiary (SPOCHUB) in Q4 FY26. PAT rose about 14% to INR 29.28 crore and EBITDA was INR 559 million at a stated 42% margin. Management said the step-up depends on the Sharon AI GPU deal (8,200 B300 GPUs in Sydney), now expected to bill from Q3 FY27 after a delay from the earlier mid-September target. Management declined to give any forward revenue or profit guidance.

segments.name: Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS)
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 51% of Q1 FY27 revenue; includes cloud IaaS, GPU IaaS and co-location. Mostly GPUs are leased from partners; no significant owned GPU capacity went live in Q1.

segments.name: Managed Services
segments.commentary: 31.31% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management said FY26 growth (about 157% YoY to about INR 76 crore) was driven by one-time technical design services for the Sharon AI cluster classified here.

segments.name: Software-as-a-Service (SaaS)
segments.commentary: 17.55% of Q1 FY27 revenue; includes Swaraj Cloud and dozens of software products. Management said SaaS was historically the higher-margin segment.

segments.name: SPOCHUB (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Recorded about INR 85 crore revenue and INR 54 crore PAT in FY26 versus near-nil in FY25, from one-time technical design services for the GPU cluster at Sharon AI. Management said this will not recur.

guidance_outlook: Management said it cannot give full-year FY27 or FY28 guidance; numbers will be disclosed quarterly.
Sharon AI GPU capacity (8,200 B300 GPUs, Sydney SYD1 data centre) expected to go live by early November 2026 per the Kunal Bajaj reply, with billing from Q1 FY28 per another reply.
Own GPU target of about 1,500 GPUs to be deployed by January-February 2027 (mid-to-end Q4 FY27).
Management targets PAT margins of 15% to 20% on GPU leasing deals.
Planned FY27 capex of about INR 1,500 crore, with a further INR 1,500 crore stated as additional capex for FY27.
Management expects the seasonality of Q4-heavy revenue to fade over the next 2-3 years as AI factories are delivered.
capex_capacity: Sharon AI deal: 8,200 latest B300 GPUs deployed in the GreenSquare SYD1 data centre in Sydney; lease locked for 7 years; the 'September 16' target slipped about 1.5 months; management now targets early November 2026 go-live.

Own GPU build-out: target about 1,500 GPUs by January-February 2027; India setup funded by IPO proceeds, customer advances and some debt in a 30:30:30 split (management said 'balance of 30-30-30' with the remainder unclear).
Management says it is not signing customers for the new India capacity yet and will buy GPUs at current prices, targeting to lease when prices rise around January.
Capex funding: customer advances of about INR 1,177 crore plus about INR 720 crore from the IPO, plus partial debt (per analyst question, confirmed by management).
Employee count 993; about 100 additions expected from the Sharon deal, with the company aiming to stay under 1,000 through churn and partner staffing.
demand_pricing: International funnel is more than 50,000 GPUs; management said customers are waiting for supply.
Domestic order book about INR 3,000 crore over a 3-year duration (per Anmol Garg question); management said domestic demand is growing at 30% to 40% CAGR.
Target lease pricing of about USD 5 to 6 per GPU per hour, in line with industry; management said pricing of B300 contracts is locked, and H100/A100 customers still pay USD 3.5 per hour.
International customers pay 12 to 18 months of advance, and management says the company prefers them for higher prices and larger down-payments.
Management says GPU supply is constrained, with delivery delays of 4 to 9 months from OEMs.
Sharon AI has reportedly leased to direct customers and now demands 50% advance per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Sharon AI go-live delayed from mid-September, and when will revenue start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the date slipped by about 1.5 months, with billing starting now. It targets early Q3 or mid-Q3, and later said November first week go-live, with billing from Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the quarterly revenue growth (7-8%) inconsistent with a 30-40% order book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonality with Q3 and Q4 stronger historically; Q1 growth of about 8% was called appropriate given domestic deliverables. Growth is expected QoQ from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GPU pricing locked for the Sharon deal and can its rate be fixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the Sharon GPU purchase cost and the customer revenue are both locked at pre-decided rates, with a 7-year contract.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 1,500 GPUs be deployed by Q4 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the target as correct, with deployment by January-February 2027 (mid-to-end Q4).

qa_highlights.question: Are there capex subsidies (PLI) or any client concentration risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not eligible for capex subsidies such as PLI. On concentration, management said advance-funded contracts reduce risk, and it did not name the clients or confirm any China exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be any deal-related guidance for FY27 or FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management declined to provide forward-looking revenue or profit figures.

risks_watch: Sharon AI go-live timing: management moved the target from mid-September to early November 2026 and gave differing billing timelines (Q3 FY27 vs Q1 FY28); track whether GreenSquare SYD1 capacity is handed over and billing starts in Q3.

Own GPU build-out of about 1,500 GPUs by January-February 2027 is unsigned to customers; management said it will buy at current prices and lease later, so exposure to GPU purchase costs and lease-up timing is open.
GPU supply constraints: management cited OEM delivery delays of 4 to 9 months, and said it relies on partner relationships to expedite deliveries.
Revenue concentration and counterparty risk: the Sharon AI deal is a single 7-year lease, and the European banking client was not named; management did not address China exposure directly.

Revenue quality: FY26 SPOCHUB design services and the Managed Services jump were described as one-time, so underlying growth (Q1 +7.28% YoY) needs to be tracked against the 30-40% domestic order book CAGR claim.
Capex funding mix (customer advances, IPO proceeds, partial debt) and the INR 1,500 crore plus INR 1,500 crore FY27 capex plan, where management did not give the amount already deployed.

summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the long-term GPU opportunity, pricing, and partner relationships, citing demand exceeding supply. It was cautious and vague on timelines, repeatedly shifting the Sharon AI go-live (mid-September, early Q3, November first week) and declining to give any FY27 or FY28 revenue or profit guidance.
